subject: Slot cascade & candidate prioritization for virtual onsite: Jordan Reynolds
messages:
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 9 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Slot cascade & candidate prioritization for virtual onsite: Jordan Reynolds

Team —

We need to lock a three-slot virtual onsite for Jordan Reynolds (applied PM role) next week and make sure we have clean panel sequencing and fallbacks. Maya (hiring manager) prefers mornings PT; candidate is east-coast but flexible in the 10a–2p PT window. High-level asks:

- Can we plan a 3-slot run (system design, cross-functional, hiring manager debrief) with 60 / 45 / 30 mins respectively?
- We should order the panels to reduce context switching for the candidate and allow shorter buffer between slots if we cascade (i.e., shorter slot first then long deep-dive).
- Need two backfill interviewers (one technical, one product) in case someone drops — ideally across time zones.

Attached: Jordan_Reynolds_Resume.pdf and a working calendar grid (panel-availability-grid.ics).

Please reply with: (A) which panel owners you can cover (B) earliest/lateset local times you can do (C) if you can be a fallback coverage.

I propose the following initial cadence (all PT):
- Slot A (30m): cross-functional scenario + culture (Tessa or Marissa)
- Slot B (60m): system design deep-dive (Karthik primary)
- Slot C (45m): hiring mgr debrief + roadmap (Maya)

Goal: get a confirmed schedule by EOD Friday so recruiter can send candidate invite.

Thanks —
Priyom
Senior Recruiter, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: Jordan_Reynolds_Resume.pdf (PDF, 92KB)]
[Attachment: panel-availability-grid.ics (calendar)]

If we cascade shorter->longer I suggest flipping A/B to 30 -> 60 -> 45 as you outlined; psychologically easier for candidate to start lighter.

Tessa Morgan

- For fallbacks, Laura can step into product debrief and I can hand off a shortened system design (40m) if we need to compress.
